prepaymentFee.title: Prepayment Fee Calculator
prepaymentFee.subtitle: Work out the fee for paying a loan off early in Korea, and what you actually keep if you refinance. Reflects the rates revised on January 13, 2025.

rateHint.before: Contracts signed before January 13, 2025 keep the old rates, so the pre-reform bank average of {rate}% is filled in. Replace it with the rate in your loan agreement.
rateHint.after: Filled in with the bank average of {rate}% for contracts from January 13, 2025 (Financial Services Commission). Rates differ by bank, so use the one in your agreement or banking app.
rateHint.bogeumjari: Cap of {rate}% per the Korea Housing Finance Corporation. Older loans keep the rate in their agreement. Waived for borrowers on the social-care or 3+ children preferential rate and for jeonse fraud victims.
rateHint.didimdol: Cap of {rate}% per the Housing and Urban Fund. Principal repaid from August 12, 2024 to December 31, 2026 is fee-free.

pay.title: Amount to repay
pay.freeHint: Some products waive the fee on up to 10% of the original loan each year (e.g. KB Kookmin Bank real-estate secured loans). If your agreement has such a clause, enter that amount.

result.label: Prepayment fee

status.charged: Day {elapsed} of the loan · {left} days left in the fee period. From {freeDate} the fee is 0.
status.free: The fee period (up to 3 years from the loan date) has ended, so there is no fee.
status.waived: Didimdol loans waive the fee on principal repaid by December 31, 2026.
status.zero: Nothing to charge (within the fee-free amount, or the rate is 0%).
status.invalid: The repayment date is before the loan start date. Please check the dates.

result.shortTerm: The loan matures within 3 years, so the fee period is the loan term ({base} days).
result.effect: Repaying {amount} KRW cuts the remaining interest by {saved} KRW and the monthly payment from {before} KRW to {after} KRW (same maturity, same rate).
result.effectNet: Even after the fee you come out {net} KRW ahead.
result.effectBullet: Repaying {amount} KRW cuts the interest until maturity by {saved} KRW, and monthly interest goes from {before} KRW to {after} KRW.

when.title: How much is the fee if you repay later?
when.desc: The later you repay the same amount, the smaller the fee, and it reaches 0 when the fee period ends.

refi.title: Is refinancing worth it?
refi.desc: Assumes the whole balance is moved to a new loan with the same repayment method, then subtracts the prepayment fee and other costs from the interest saved.
refi.costsHint: Add costs you pay yourself, such as releasing the old mortgage lien, the discount on mandatory housing bonds or guarantee fees. For bank mortgages the lien registration costs (registration tax, legal fees) and appraisal fee are usually paid by the bank.
refi.stampNote: Stamp duty on a {amount} KRW loan is {total} KRW, split evenly with the bank. Loans of 50 million KRW or less are exempt.
refi.breakEven: After {n} months the interest saved exceeds the costs.
refi.noBreakEven: The interest saved never covers the fee and costs.
refi.longer: A longer term lowers the monthly payment but can raise total interest. Compare with the new term equal to the remaining term too.

wait.title: What if you wait until the fee disappears?
wait.nowBetter: Refinancing now leaves you {diff} KRW more: the extra interest while waiting is larger than the fee.
wait.laterBetter: Waiting leaves you {diff} KRW more: the fee is larger than the extra interest while waiting.
wait.note: Assumes both rates stay the same and the maturity is unchanged if you wait.

refi.note: A new loan goes through LTV and DSR screening again. Use rates you actually got quoted in a banking app or a loan-switching comparison service.

rates.title: Prepayment fee rates by loan type
rates.desc: Bank averages are the figures the Financial Services Commission published with the January 2025 reform. Actual rates vary by bank and product and are recalculated every year.

tips.title: Good to know
items: A prepayment fee can only be charged if you repay within 3 years of the loan date (Financial Consumer Protection Act, Article 20). After 3 years it is 0 whenever you repay.
Loans signed from January 13, 2025 may only charge actual costs (lost returns on funds plus administrative and origination costs). Older contracts keep their original rates.
The fee shrinks a little every day. If only a few months of the fee period remain, waiting may pay off.
When refinancing, weigh not only the rate gap but also the prepayment fee, stamp duty, lien release and registration costs, and the new loan's own 3-year fee period.

Withdrawing a loan contract (Financial Consumer Protection Act, Article 46, within 14 days of receiving the contract documents, etc.) waives the prepayment fee. There is a cap on the loan amount that can be withdrawn, so check with your bank.
